A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same shallow ReLU-like loss-landscape study, with matching central theorems, experiments and embedding analysis. Their text, equations, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original GD training trajectories, experiments with two initialization scales, and a 5,000-perturbation local-minimum check (Section 4 and Appendices G and L).

after.justification: V5 retains these empirical results and adds original higher-dimensional input and vector-output experiments, including parameter trajectories, residual analysis and another perturbation check (Appendix I).

M1.justification: The studied architecture, ReLU-like activations, squared loss, GD procedure and network-embedding operations remain unchanged. V5 explicitly identifies its directional-stationarity formulation as equivalent to the existing conditions; the additional theory and experiments do not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: V2's neural-network experiments use five two-dimensional inputs with scalar targets. V5 retains this coverage and adds seven-sample three-dimensional-input/scalar-output and four-sample two-dimensional-input/vector-output regression problems (Appendix I), substantially extending the represented input and output settings.

E2.justification: Neither version reports empirical comparisons against competing algorithms. V5's added comparisons with Clarke and canonical-axis stationarity concern mathematical definitions, rather than experimentally evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The retained main experiment keeps 50 hidden neurons, 500k epochs, step size 0.001 and initialization standard deviation 5e-6. The added Appendix I experiments retain 50 neurons but use standard deviation 9.51e-11 and trajectories extending to approximately 600k and 300k epochs (Figures 11–12). These are additional settings, not revisions of the original runs.

E4.justification: Appendix I.2 adds a substantial analysis of successive vector-output saddles, using component residuals and approximate derivative calculations to identify escape neurons and investigate neuron splitting. It also adds a separate 5,000-perturbation local-minimum check. The original initialization-sensitivity study and scalar-output perturbation analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed replication, confidence intervals or significance tests. V5 applies the existing 5,000-random-perturbation and histogram practice to another experiment; this adds results without changing the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: V5 adds a three-dimensional-input trajectory with four saddle escapes and reported zero final loss, plus a vector-output trajectory with three escapes, neuron splitting and a final underfitting local minimum (Appendix I, Figures 11–14). The original experimental plots and findings are retained unchanged. These additions are results under new settings, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The central Theorem 4.2 and embedding Proposition 4.8 remain intact. V5 adds Proposition C.1 and its GD escape-time proof, Proposition C.6 and Fact C.7 connecting directional and Clarke stationarity, and a counterexample to canonical-axis stationarity. Corollary 4.6 also formalizes the restriction on saddles approached from vanishing initialization.

C1.justification: V2 presents proposed stationarity conditions; v5 explicitly identifies the established directional-stationarity notion and emphasizes its suitability for characterizing GD stagnation. The escape-neuron and embedding contributions remain stable. Excluding alternative scalar-output saddle-escape mechanisms was already claimed in v2 Section 4.2.

C2.justification: V5 substantially expands the rationale and boundaries of its stationarity notion, including exceptional GD-stalling points it can miss (Appendix C). It explains the higher-order proof difficulty behind restricting the main theorem to shallow networks and interprets vector-output escape through nonzero output-weight cancellation and neuron splitting (Section 4.1 and Appendix I.2).

D1.justification: V5 documents the exact input and target arrays, network widths and initialization distributions for the added experiments. Its reproducibility statement replaces v2's anonymous repository pointer with a GitHub code pointer. The implementation information for the retained main experiment is essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: V5 substantially expands its positioning within nonsmooth optimization through comparisons involving directional, Clarke and canonical-axis stationarity, citing works including Li et al. (2020), Clarke (1975), Davis et al. (2020) and Yun et al. (2019). Kumar and Haupt (2024) also becomes central to the saddle-dynamics positioning. These changes exceed citation-format updates.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, stationarity discussion and training-dynamics narrative are extensively rewritten. V5 adds Section 3.2.1 and an appendix contents list, moves the larger-initialization discussion into Appendices J–K, and relocates embedding applications to Appendix Q. This substantially reorganizes retained material as well as accommodating additions.

P2.justification: V5 adds the aligned-coordinate illustration in Figure 9 and the training, perturbation and residual displays in Figures 11–14. It revises the flowchart labels, relocates the larger-initialization plots from v2 Figure 5 to v5 Figure 15, and adopts a substantially different conference layout. The retained experimental plot contents are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V5 improves conceptual grounding and research positioning through Section 3.2.1 and Appendix C, while Appendix I illustrates important multidimensional behavior absent from v2. These are useful gains in explanation and support for the retained central results. However, the new worked validation contains numerical inconsistencies: Appendix I.2 states e12 = +0.12 near epoch 100k, whereas Figure 14b shows it as negative. This limits the reliability of the added quantitative explanation and qualifies the overall improvement.
